newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 124,000t corn, 156,000t soy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 124,000t corn, 156,000t soy.

text.p: Falling futures prices in the U.S. could prompt Taiwan to tender for up to 124,000 tonnes of corn and 156,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, traders said on Friday.

"No detailed plan has yet been announced, but with U.S. corn and soybean futures prices continuing to fall, tenders for one or two 54,000-tonne shipments for corn and soybeans each are very likely next week," an executive at Zennoh Grain said.
The Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) December corn futures contract touched a 14-month session low of US$2.65-1.2 a bushel on Thursday before ending 4-1/4 U.S. cents down at $2.66.
The CBOT November soybeans contract skidded 21-3/4 U.S. cents to end yesterday at $6.67-3/4 a bushel. Corn and soybean futures prices have declined by over $1 a bushel since July.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group was expected to tender for a combined shipment of 16,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said. The Hui Shung Group's shipment would be slated for delivery in March.
Taiwan's Flour Mills Association would be sidelined next week despite falling U.S. wheat futures prices because of ample stocks, association director Lu Wei-chin said.
"Despite the falling U.S. wheat futures, we have no immediate plan next week to buy wheat because Taiwan still has plenty of wheat stocks," Lu said.
"We do have plans to buy wheat in the near future, but details have yet to be set," he said.
The association bought two shipments totalling 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on October 11.
Taiwan's soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was quoted at T$9.50-$9.70 a kg, down from $9.60-$9.80 last week.
The price of corn powders was at $6.70-$6.80 per kg for Taipei delivery, down from $6.95 a week earlier.
The local flour price listed on Friday was seen between $14.55-$15.68/kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
The U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan freight cost was about US$10.50 per tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico about $18.00 to $19.00 per tonne, both for Panamax-sized January and February shipments.
